newsitem.title: JAPAN: Recent yen rise not overly excessive - MOF official.
newsitem.headline: Recent yen rise not overly excessive - MOF official.

text.p: The recent rise of the yen is not overly excessive and is within the expected market reaction to the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' agreement in Washington last month, an official of Japan's Finance Ministry told Reuters on Monday.
The official spoke in the city of Fukuoka, where he was attending the annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank.
Asked whether the recent rise of the yen was excessive and too rapid, the official said:
"No, I don't think so. It appears to be within the reaction the market was expected to show to the G7 agreement made in Washington."
The G7 nations issued a joint statement in Washington on April 27 saying that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excessive volatility in currency markets was undesirable.
They also emphasised the importance of avoiding exchange rates that would create large external imbalances and agreed to to cooperate as appropriate in foreign exchange markets.
